newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NSW coal miners threaten strike.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NSW coal miners threaten strike.

text.p: Coal miners in the Australian state of New South Wales are threatening to strike from later on Thursday because of a cut in accident compensation, a senior union official said on Thursday.

"Our members will not be attending for work if their methods of compensation for injury are going to be severely reduced," John Maitland, the National President of the Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU), told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
"Absolutely," Maitland said if the union was threatening industrial action.

"I'm having great difficulty in holding back on this particular issue right now. We're giving the industry until 1 p.m. (0200 GMT) to reconsider their position because they were the ones that have lobbied the opposition," Maitland said.
The upper house of the New South Wales parliament voted late on Wednesday to include coal miners in plans to cut lump sum compensation payments for seriously injured workers.
The Labor government, which controls the lower house but not the upper house, originally excluded coal miners from the cuts.
The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and CRA Ltd have significant coal mining operations in the Hunter Valley region in central New South Wales.
